content.comment_body: Good morning, I'm having some trouble with a voltage analogue input on my [product_name]. In the simulation tool, everything seems to work as expected, but on the actual hardware, I don't get the correct readings. The input voltage ranges from 0 to 5 volts, sourced from a temperature sensor. The goal is for the PLC to trigger an output whenever the voltage drops below about 1.5 volts. Although I measured 4.3 volts at the input, the online test shows a value of '0'. I've attached the relevant section of the program. Could someone review it and suggest where I might be mistaken? Any help is appreciated, Best regards, [user_name].

Hello [user_name], You need to adjust the settings in the main menu of [product_name] software to enable either two or four analogue inputs. Also, please provide the complete model number for your device.

Hi, Thank you for your response. Model: [article_no] DC 12/24v inputs x 6 DC I1, I2 are AI3, AI4 (0-10v) I7, I8 are AI1, AI2 (0-10v) In the rest of the program, I use digital inputs on the other channels. Would it still be possible to use inputs 1-8 (excluding #2) as digital inputs, even though input #2 is set to analogue mode in the configuration? Thanks, [user_name].

Go to: Bestand > Eigenschappen (ALT + Enter) In the parameters section at the bottom of the screen, you will find settings for AI3/DI1 and AI4/DI2. I hope this helps. Sorry, instructions are in Dutch only....

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter issues with analogue input behavior on [product_name] when moving from simulation to actual hardware testing. While readings appear accurate in simulation, the real device fails to register expected values, instead displaying '0' despite measurable voltage at the input. There is uncertainty regarding configuration and related parameter settings for switching between analogue and digital modes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect analogue input functionality to remain consistent across both simulation and physical device scenarios, with proper configuration to support combined use of analogue and digital inputs as needed.
